basics.notice: Listen to مَلِكِ, قُلْ and بِرَبِّ: the open a of مَ, the closed لْ with no vowel, and the doubled بِّ, said twice.

istiadha.notice: 16:98 commands the استعاذة before reciting; the words you say are أَعُوذُ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ, which are not themselves an ayah. Then listen to 9:1, التوبة, the one surah that starts with no بسملة.

tabii.notice: Listen to the و in أَعُوذُ, the small ا in إِلَٰهِ and the ي in ٱلَّذِينَ: each is held for exactly two counts, twice a short vowel.

arid.notice: Listen to the end of ٱلنَّاسِ, ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ and تَعْلَمُونَ when the reciter stops: the ا، ي or و before the last letter may be held 2, 4 or 6 counts; all three are correct.

iwad.notice: Listen to the stop on أَفْوَاجًا: the تنوين is dropped and the word ends on a two-count ا.

lam-q.notice: Listen to the ل in ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ, ٱلْحَمْدُ and وَٱلْقَمَرِ: it is said clearly, with سكون, before the next letter.

lam-s.notice: Listen to ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ, وَٱلسَّٰبِحَٰتِ and ٱلصِّرَٰطَ: the ل of ال is silent and the next letter is doubled.

ibtida.notice: Listen to how the reciter starts ٱلَّذِى, ٱهْدِنَا and ٱدْعُ: the ٱ is said, with a فتحة, a كسرة or a ضمة. In Say you will hear it disappear when the word is joined.

tafkhim.notice: Listen to the خ in ٱلْخَنَّاسِ, the قَا in ٱلْقَارِعَةُ and the قِ in ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ: the mouth fills and the sound is full and deep, strongest with a فتحة and an ا, weakest with a كسرة.

lam-jh.notice: Listen to the ل of the name in هُوَ ٱللَّهُ, in ٱللَّهُ at the start of an ayah, and in رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ: after a فتحة or a ضمة, and when you start on it, it is heavy and full.

lam-jl.notice: Listen to the ل of the name in لِلَّهِ, دِينِ ٱللَّهِ and قُلِ ٱللَّهُمَّ: after a كسرة, even one added to join the words, it is light and thin.

ghunnah.notice: Listen to the نّ in ٱلْجِنَّةِ and إِنَّ and the مّ in عَمَّ: a nasal hum is held for two counts.

izhar.notice: Listen to حَاسِدٍ إِذَا, أَنْعَمْتَ and مَنْ خَافَ: the ن or تنوين is said clearly and the voice moves straight on to the throat letter, with no held hum.

idgh-g.notice: Listen to فَمَن يَعْمَلْ, نَفْسٌ مَّا and فَلَن نَّزِيدَكُمْ: the ن or تنوين disappears into the next letter and a two-count غنة carries it.

idgh-n.notice: Listen to عَن رَّبِّهِمْ, أَن لَّمْ and خَيْرٌ لَّكَ: the ن or تنوين merges into the ر or ل completely, with no غنة at all.

iqlab.notice: Listen to مَنۢ بَخِلَ, فَأَنۢبَتْنَا and كِرَامٍۭ بَرَرَةٍ: the ن or تنوين turns into a hidden م on the lips, with a two-count غنة before the ب.

ikhfa.notice: Listen to مِن شَرِّ, أَنتُمْ and نَارًا ذَاتَ: the ن or تنوين is hidden, and a two-count غنة carries the sound into the next letter.

qal-s.notice: Listen to يَلِدْ, يَدْخُلُونَ and حَبْلٌ: the قلقلة letter with a سكون gives a small bounce as it is released, without a vowel.

qal-k.notice: Listen to the stop on ٱلْفَلَقِ, أَحَدٌ and وَقَبَ: the last letter loses its vowel and bounces more strongly than in the middle of a word.

muttasil.notice: Listen to جَآءَ, سُوٓءَ and سِىٓءَ: the ا, و or ي before a همزة in the same word is held four or five counts.

munfasil.notice: Listen to لَآ أَعْبُدُ, فِىٓ أَحْسَنِ and قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّ: the ا, ي or و at the end of one word is held long before the همزة that starts the next.

mithlayn.notice: Listen to هَل لَّكَ, ٱذْهَب بِّكِتَٰبِى and رَبِحَت تِّجَٰرَتُهُمْ: the two identical letters become one doubled letter, with no break between them.

mutajanisayn.notice: Listen to عَبَدتُّمْ: the د is not said; it becomes the ت, which is doubled.

sakinayn.notice: Listen to فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ, بَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ and ذُو ٱلْعَرْشِ: a حرف مد before ال is not said, and any other ساكن takes a vowel.

m-izhar.notice: Listen to the مْ in أَلَمْ تَرَ: the lips close once, cleanly, with no held hum.

m-idgham.notice: Listen to أَطْعَمَهُم مِّن: the two م become one doubled م with a two-count غنة.

m-ikhfa.notice: Listen to تَرْمِيهِم بِحِجَارَةٍ: the م before ب is hidden with a held غنة on the lips.

silent-letters.notice: Listen to فَلْيَعْبُدُوا۟: the ا after the و is written but never said. In أَنَا۠, joined, the ا is not said either.

silah-s.notice: Listen to وَإِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ: the هـ of the pronoun is stretched two counts, like a small و, because the letters on both sides of it have vowels.

silah-k.notice: Listen to مَالَهُۥٓ أَخْلَدَهُۥ: the pronoun's و is held four or five counts before the همزة.

badal.notice: Listen to ءَامَنُوا۟: the ا after the همزة is only two counts, though a همزة is next to it.

lin.notice: Listen to the stop on قُرَيْشٍ: the يْ after a فتحة glides softly, and the reciter may stretch it before the last letter.

ra-h.notice: Listen to the ر in رَبَّكَ and زُرْتُمُ: full and heavy, like the heavy letters.

ra-l.notice: Listen to the ر in ٱلْخَيْرِ and وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ: thin and light, with or after a كسرة.

aqwa-maddayn.notice: Listen to رِئَآءَ: the ا has a همزة before it (بدل) and after it (متصل); the stronger متصل wins, four or five counts.

dad-zha.notice: Listen to أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ: the ض runs along the side of the tongue, then the ظ comes from the tip at the teeth.

lazim-k.notice: Listen to ضَآلًّا: the ا before the شدة is held a full six counts, joined or stopping.

lazim-h.notice: Listen to the letter names in الٓمٓ: لام and ميم are each held six counts.

mutaqaribayn.notice: Listen to وَقُل رَّبِّ and بَل رَّفَعَهُ: the ل is not said and the ر is doubled. In نَخْلُقكُّم the ق goes into the ك.

waqf-signs.notice: Look at the small sign over قَوْلُهُمْ ۘ: a stop there is required, and joining could suggest a wrong meaning. Each sign tells you whether a pause is required, allowed, better or forbidden.

waqf-how.notice: Listen to the last word at each stop: ٱلْمُزَّمِّلُ ends in a سكون, أَبَدًا ends in a long ا, and ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ ends in a soft هـ.

rawm-ishmam.notice: The reciters here stop on أَحَدٌ and ٱلْأَكْرَمُ with a plain سكون. الروم (a third of the vowel, whispered) is heard only from close by, and الإشمام (the lips round after the سكون) is seen, not heard: watch a teacher's lips.

sakt.notice: Listen to بَلْ ۜ رَانَ and مَنْ ۜ رَاقٍ: the voice stops for a moment with no breath, so the ل and the ن stay clear instead of merging into the ر.

imalah.notice: Listen to مَجْر۪ىٰهَا: the رَا is tilted toward رِي (إمالة كبرى), the only such word in حفص.

ishmam.notice: Listen to تَأْمَ۫نَّا: one merged, doubled ن with its غنة. The الإشمام is seen, not heard: watch a teacher's lips round on the merged ن.

tashil.notice: Listen to ءَا۬عْجَمِىٌّ: the second همزة is softened, between a همزة and an ا.

makharij-jawf.notice: Listen to the long vowels in قَالُوا۟، دُونِ، نَذِيرٌ, and in بَا، بُو، بِي: they come from the open space of the mouth and throat, with no contact.

makharij-halq.notice: Listen to the throat letters in أَحْسَنُ، يَخْشَوْنَ، أَهْدَىٰٓ, and in أَءْ، أَهْ، أَعْ، أَحْ، أَغْ، أَخْ: each starts at a different depth of the throat.

makharij-aqsa.notice: Listen to ق and ك in وَيَقْبِضْنَ، تَوَكَّلْنَا، ٱلْأَكْبَرَ, and in أَقْ and أَكْ: the back of the tongue touches the palate, ق further back than ك.

makharij-wasat.notice: Listen to يّ، جْ، شْ in تَمَيَّزُ، وَجْهِهِۦٓ، تَشْكُرُونَ, and to أَجْ، أَشْ، أَيْ and أَضْ: the middle and the side of the tongue at work.

makharij-taraf.notice: Listen to the tip of the tongue in ٱلدُّنْيَا، نَسْمَعُ، فَكَذَّبْنَا, and in أَنْ، أَرْ and أَتْ، أَدْ، أَطْ: each made at a slightly different spot.

makharij-shafatan.notice: Listen to the lips in أَمْسَكَ، صَٰٓفَّٰتٍ، وُجُوهُ, and in أَفْ، أَبْ، أَمْ، أَوْ: the lips, and the hum from the nose in م and ن.

sifat-hams.notice: Listen to the breath in يَخْسِفَ، فَسُحْقًا، مُّسْتَقِيمٍ, and in أَفْ and أَبْ: a flow of breath with the first, the breath held back with the second.

sifat-shidda.notice: Listen to قَدْ، وَأَعْتَدْنَا، تُحْشَرُونَ, and to أَبْ, أَلْ and أَسْ: the sound stops, half-flows, or runs freely.

sifat-istila.notice: Listen to the heavy letters in ٱلصُّدُورِ، ٱلْغَيْظِ، خَلَقَ, and to أَصْ and أَسْ: the same place, but the tongue rises and covers in ص.

sifat-safir.notice: Listen to أَصْبَحَ، يَنقَلِبْ، ٱلْمَوْتَ: a whistle, a bounce, and a soft لين; and to أَصْ، أَزْ، أَسْ: a whistle runs through the front teeth.

sifat-inhiraf.notice: Listen to كَرَّتَيْنِ، كُلِّ، لِّلشَّيَٰطِينِ, and to أَرْ and أَشْ: the ر does not trill; the ش spreads through the mouth.

maratib.notice: The same rules at three speeds: every length and غنة stays, only the pace changes.
